names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 23 iunie, «Sfântul Mucenic Aristocleu, preotul»; the form is the bare name, the rest of the line being rank and office.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Αριστοκλής ο πρεσβύτερος, Δημητριανός διάκονος και Αθανάσιος αναγνώστης», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 20. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученици Аристокл, Димитријан и Атанасије“ — Свети is not a rank and мученици is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off and the first of the three bare forenames is left, which is all the heading gives him. «of Tamassos» in the display name is the corpus’s own disambiguation off another book and is not in this heading. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Аристокл», so there is no fold — worth having measured, the corpus keeping an `aristocles-of-moscow` and an `aristocleus-of-tamassos` whose slugs are one letter apart.

Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 20 июня ст. ст., «Аристоклий Саламинский (Кипрский), пресвитер, сщмч.», with the grade and rank words left off; the parenthetical form and the epithets are the calendar's own.

death.note: Two books, two readings, and the field is widened rather than chosen. doxologia’s life places his death in the persecution it dates «împăratului Maximian Galeriu (285-305)»; that interval is the reign the page prints, no closer year being given, and it is what this field held before. The Охридски пролог for 20. јун ст. ст. ends the entry „после истјазања Аристокла мачем посеку, а Димитријана и Атанасија у огњу спале 306. године“ — in the year 306, one year outside that interval, so the field now holds both and the display names both. saint.gr’s own narrative says «Το 302 μ.Χ.», which falls inside the widened field. Nothing is averaged and no book is preferred (5 October 2026).

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's serbian row carries; its greek row stands on 23 June, which is that calendar's own day for the company and not a second Russian feast. The one life page days.pravoslavie.ru gives the three, life1352, heads «День памяти: 20 июня» and names no other day; it was read whole and its account agrees with what this folder already carries — Tamassos, the flight to the cave, the light and the command to return, the meeting at the church of the apostle Barnabas, the preaching at Salamis, the fire that did not touch two of them, and the beheading about 306 — so no paragraph was added. It names the persecution as that of Maximian Galerius, 305 to 311, and heads all three «Саламинский (Кипрский)» where this corpus has read the presbyter's own town, Tamassos, into the display names.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it is plainly the same man: the presbyter from Tamassos in Cyprus who hid in a cave on a mountain, came down to Salamis after a vision, and was beheaded with a deacon and a reader. Against the corpus's two other men of the name — Aristocles of Moscow and Aristokles the Athonite — the see and the century settle it. The page's heading reads «(; - 302)» and its narrative «Το 302 μ.Χ.», which falls inside the 285–305 bracket the folder's `dates` already carry, so no change to `dates` is proposed. The Greek line names his two companions, whom the corpus did not keep; they are new folders in the same day's batch. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn under their line.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.07.2026 (20. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Аристокл, Димитријан и Атанасије“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the first of its three men. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **AN ENUMERATED COMPANY OF THREE, AND ALL THREE HAVE FOLDERS.** §5 counts what the heading enumerates: three names, Аристокл, Димитријан and Атанасије, therefore three rows and no folder. `ls saints | grep -iE 'aristocl|demetrian|athanasius'` turned up `aristocleus-of-tamassos`, `demetrianus-the-deacon` and `athanasius-the-reader`, already relating one another in all six directions, and the identification is made on the scene and not on the name: a priest of Tamassus on Cyprus, a deacon and a reader, going down together to Salamis of Cyprus and martyred there. **THE DAY IS NOT THE SAME NUMBER, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING.** The Romanian and Greek rows on these three folders are all **23 June**; this book keeps them on the **20th**, three days earlier. That is not a §4 second-day note, which is owed only where a folder already carries a venerated row **for this same church** on another day, and the `serbian` row was `undocumented` on all three. The row goes on the day the page read is, which is 20 June, and the three-day difference is a reading recorded here and in no field. **THE DATE IS WIDENED, AND ACROSS A DASH.** The folder held `death` 285 to 305, display «285–305», off doxologia’s «împăratului Maximian Galeriu (285-305)» — an interval that is itself a reign the page printed. This book ends the entry „а Димитријана и Атанасија у огњу спале 306. године“, in the year 306, which is **one year outside** that interval. Two books, two readings, and the rule is to widen and not to choose: `death` earliest 285, latest 306, display **«285–305 or 306»**, basis traditional, both sentences in the note. The compound takes the dash form the rule names for exactly this shape, a stated range beside a second reading, as «286–305 or about 308» does. Nothing is averaged, neither book is preferred, and **the one-year overshoot is not smoothed away** by preferring the interval that nearly holds it. saint.gr’s own 302 falls inside the widened field and is not in the display, because it is in that page’s narrative and not in what this field’s note cited when it was written. **A VOICE FROM HEAVEN WHERE THE GREEK PAGE HAD A VISION, AND NO CAVE AT ALL.** „Због његове велике ревности к вери удостоји се гласа с неба, да иде у Саламину Кипарску и прими венац мучеништва“ — for his great zeal for the faith he was counted worthy of a voice from heaven, that he should go to Salamis of Cyprus and receive the crown of martyrdom. saint.gr had a vision and a reasoning from it; doxologia had the mountain and the cave and the church of the Apostle Barnabas on the road. **This book has no cave, no mountain and no Barnabas**, and it has the destination and the crown named in the voice itself. Both are written and neither is chosen, and an omission is not a disagreement. This is the **second voice from heaven in two days** of this wave, after the one in the middle of Zosimus’s torments on 19 June. `ls saints | grep -i barnab` is not reached for: no folder takes a row off a book that does not name him. THE CATHEDRAL CHURCH, WHICH IS NEW AND IS NOT AN `office`. „Аристокл би свештеник саборне цркве у граду Тамасу на Кипру“ — priest of the **cathedral** church of Tamassus, where doxologia said only a priest in the town. **No `office` is invented from it**: offices go through the packs’ `offices` branch, whose keys are English phrases the data already wrote down, and no pack holds «Priest of the cathedral church of Tamassus». The folder’s `office` stays null and the reading is in the life. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND THE BODY’S RANK WORD IS REFUSED. „Свети мученици“ is the heading’s only rank and gives `martyr`, which all three folders carry. „свештеник“ stands in the **body**, and a rank inferred from the body is not written — the folder carries `presbyter` already, off another book’s heading, and it is left exactly as it was rather than confirmed from a body. No `locations`. **No new rows**: the three already relate one another, and the governor is unnamed here. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FIFTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети Левкије, епископ врунтисиопољски, у Италији“ — Leucius, born in Alexandria, early into a monastery, counted worthy of great revelations and of a mighty grace, so that he raised the dead and drove demons out of men; bishop first in Alexandria, then by a command from heaven crossing into Italy to the pagan city of Vruntisiopolj, which he baptised whole and in which he built a church of the Mother of God; and after much and successful labour passing over into eternity in the time of the emperor Theodosius II, in the fifth century. **Three folders hold the name and not one of them is he.** `ls saints | grep -i leuci` returns exactly three: `leucius-of-caesarea`, a martyr of 249–251 kept with Thyrsus and Coronatus, who is not a bishop and not of Italy; `leucius-companion-of-peter`, a martyr kept with Peter and Severus on the Greek 11 January; and `leucius-of-volokolamsk`, a Russian. `ls saints | grep -iE 'brundis|brindis'` returns nobody at all. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the fifth century, Theodosius II and the city are written nowhere**, because there is nothing to write them on. The day’s verse is his, and a verse is not a hymn and not a folder either. THE DAY’S SIXTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Блажени Студије“ — Studius, a notable patrician and consul in Constantinople, who founded near the Golden Gate the church of Saint John the Forerunner and the monastery called the Studion after him; a house that became famous for many glorious men, spiritual fathers, ascetics and sufferers for the faith; destroyed by the Latin crusaders in 1204, restored by the emperor Constantine Palaeologus Porphyrogenitus in 1293, and with a Turkish mosque standing on the place now. `ls saints | grep -i studi` returns five folders and **every one of them is a Studite and not the Studius the house is named after** — `damascene-the-studite`, `james-of-studion`, `naucratius-the-studite`, `nicholas-the-studite`, `theodore-the-studite`. The last of those is the man this entry names as the house’s most famous son, and **he takes no row and no mention in any prose written today**: a founder’s monastery is a dedication and a later inhabitant of it is not a relation. Ruling 3 on Studius himself: named here, no folder from me, and **1204, 1293 and the consulship are written nowhere**. The Блажени of his heading therefore decides nothing, there being no folder for it to decide a type on; had there been one it would still be the §5 reading «fool-for-christ *or* righteous — read which», and a patrician and consul who founds a monastery is neither obviously.
